correctness.rationale: Independently rebuilt the integer compressed-walk matrix B for each half-separation from the coin/shift, keeping the full ordered matrix-unit space rather than using the frozen symmetry reduction. For each B its exact characteristic polynomial P(z) is coprime with z^deg(P) P(2/z); a root of modulus sqrt(2) would supply a common root by conjugation. As B/sqrt(2) is a contraction, this certifies strict spectral radius less than one and geometric survival tails. Using F=2I-B^T⊗B^T, solved Fv=2vec(I) and Fw=2v exactly over the rationals; at the index of the initial diagonal matrix unit, v gives the mean and 2w-v the second moment. Obtained (mean, second, variance, slope) equal to (1,1,0,0), (4,24,8,2), (9,145,64,4), and (16,560,304,-32). A single, zero-cost reset attempt succeeds with generating-function weight f(1-r)/(1-r), and lasts on average [1-f(1-r)]/r; expansion gives (mean^2-mean-variance)/2. The quotient as written applies for 0<r<1; at r=1 with L>1 detection is impossible, and L=1 is always detected in one step. This endpoint does not alter the stated weak-reset finding. The classical Dirichlet equations give m_1(x)=L^2-x^2 and m_2(x)=(x^4+(2-6L^2)x^2+5L^4-2L^2)/3, so the slopes are 0,2,12,40. Replay is given by the backward linear systems above and the specified basis and one-step coefficients in RESULT.md; frozen verify_variance.py was inspected, not run. No claim is checked beyond the four sizes or about a global optimum.

evidence: An equality of no-reset means cannot settle the required reset derivative because the second moment enters with independent sign. The no-reset operator provides the starting point, but four distinct rational second-moment systems have to be evaluated and signed.

searches: Wójcik arXiv:2510.27377v2 Eq. (16) and Appendix B

evidence: Wójcik uses the same unreset walk and localized initial state. His K0=sqrt(1-p)U and reset Kraus operators are alternative branches per counted step. His Appendix B gives a restarted mean for L=5.

Embedding his updates at successive unitary moves recovers Bernoulli reset of the incoming state between moves with probability p, but actual elapsed iterations include the skipped moves. His mean equals the zero-time-reset mean divided by 1-p under this coupling; consequently the weak slope adds the no-reset mean.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The effect of time counting is a concrete algebraic distinction even when the embedded trajectory agrees. The L=5 formula does not give an L=1–4 table or its first improving width.

value.rationale: The four consecutive smallest widths are an exhaustive, motivated search for the onset of a qualitative sign reversal, not arbitrary table entries. The matched classical calculation shows that equal no-reset mean times can coexist with opposite local reset effects. The precise threshold is useful when selecting small benchmark systems; the value is limited to this coin, preparation, monitoring and reset rule.
